Details:
a. Standardization: Convert features to a distribution with a mean of 0 and standard deviation of 1. Important for SVM and neural networks due to sensitivity to feature scale.
b. Normalization: Scale feature values to between 0 and 1 to speed up model convergence, especially in neural networks.

a. Based on feature importance: Use random forest or GBM to calculate feature importance and select the most important features.
b. Principal component analysis (PCA): Reduce dimensionality by converting features into principal components, retaining main information. Useful for SVM and neural networks.

a. Feature combination: Combine existing features to create new interactive features, capturing complex relationships. Effective for GBM and neural networks.
b. Polynomial features: Expand feature space by generating polynomial features (e.g., square, cube). Works well in SVM with kernel functions.

Applicable Models: SVM, Random Forest, GBM, Neural Network
Details: Category encoding (One-Hot Encoding): Convert non-numeric categorical features into numerical features. Important for neural networks and SVM.
Interpolation or filling missing values: Use mean, median, or nearest neighbor methods to fill in missing values, avoiding errors during training.
